title: Analysis, Uncertainty & Reporting
description: Study repeated runs and variability, effect sizes and confidence intervals, error analysis and subgroup behavior, and negative results and limitations. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Repeated runs and variability
lessons.description: Summarize all runs and identify the sources of variation.
lessons.conceptOverview: Report variability across appropriate repeated runs rather than selecting only the best seed. Distinguish variation from initialization, data sampling and evaluation uncertainty.
lessons.whyItMatters: Single-run wins may not represent reliable improvement.

lessons.title: Effect sizes and confidence intervals
lessons.description: Report the absolute change and its relevance to the service objective.
lessons.conceptOverview: An effect size describes the magnitude of a difference; an interval expresses uncertainty under its assumptions. Statistical significance alone does not establish practical usefulness.
lessons.whyItMatters: Practical importance and statistical evidence are different questions.

lessons.title: Error analysis and subgroup behavior
lessons.description: Create a length-stratified analysis and inspect representative errors.
lessons.conceptOverview: Inspect failures by meaningful categories to understand mechanisms and limits. Avoid inventing explanations from a few anecdotes; use examples to motivate checks on a broader sample.
lessons.whyItMatters: Aggregate gains can hide important subgroup regressions.

lessons.title: Negative results and limitations
lessons.description: State what the result rules out and what remains unresolved.
lessons.conceptOverview: A negative result can constrain a hypothesis when the experiment was capable of detecting the relevant effect. Report scope, uncertainty and implementation checks rather than claiming universal impossibility.
lessons.whyItMatters: Absence of detected improvement is not always evidence of no possible effect.
